Alex: Heads up — seeing a 3x tail latency increase on the dedicated us-west-2c pool since 08:20 UTC. Short gen requests (<=512 tokens) are spiking to 600-800ms p95. Suspect noisy tenant + long prompts + streaming interplay.
Priya: Do we have traces and kernel-selection logs?
Alex: Trace: https://traces.internal/r/8a3f2b — shows lots of small batches choosing the small-batch kernel, then falling back to generic on next stage. Attaching profiling snapshot (GPU stall/ memcpy) and scheduler logs.
Mateo: I pulled the kernel-selection log. Key snippet: `kernel_selector: chosen=SMALL_BATCH_KERNEL reason='batch_size_predicted<=8' actual_seq=10240 expected_seq=256`. So selector used batch-optimized kernel because batch size tiny, but ignored sequence-length distribution -> leads to terrible tile/memory behavior.
Julia: We're also seeing KV-cache eviction storms for tenant-99. Eviction rate jumped 7x right when burst starts. That causes extra GPU-to-host memcpy and invalidates prefix caches.
observability-bot: alert: dedicated-usw2c latency-p95 > 600ms (08:20-08:28), tenant-99 request_rate=220r/min, avg_prompt_length=45200 tokens.
ops-oncall: Can we throttle tenant-99 briefly while we triage? They are on a burst plan but this is impacting others.
Alex: +1 to throttling. Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) soft throttle tenant-99 to 50r/min, 2) pin kernel selector heuristic to consider `expected_total_seq_len` so very-large-seq uses large-seq kernel, 3) increase kvcache budget per-tenant on that node temporarily.
Priya: For a quick check I ran `grep kernel_selector logs | tail -n50` and saw ~92% matches of the wrong branch during the incident window. Sharing the grep output: 
```
2026-03-18T08:21:03Z kernel_selector: predicted_batch=3 predicted_seq=128 choose=SMALL_BATCH_KERNEL
2026-03-18T08:21:04Z kernel_selector: actual_seq=32768 cache_eviction=true fallback=GENERIC_KERNEL
...
```
Mateo: I have a small patch ready that changes selector to use `effective_seq = max(predicted_seq, median_recent_seq)` and avoids SMALL_BATCH_KERNEL if `effective_seq > 2048`. Test run in staging shows p95 drop from 750ms -> 220ms for mixed workloads. Commit sha: a1b2c3d (branch: fix/kernelselect-longseq).
deploy-bot: Scheduled canary deploy of a1b2c3d to us-west-2c at 08:45 UTC.
Julia: Also recommend we tune batching heuristic: prefer batch consolidation when many concurrent streams share prefix to avoid per-request kernel thrash. I'll open a follow-up PR for batching policy.
ops-oncall: Throttle applied to tenant-99 at 08:30 UTC (50r/min). Latency p95 dropped to ~280ms at 08:36 — still above baseline but much better.
Alex: Good. Action items: (1) roll canary and monitor kernel-selection metrics, (2) increase per-tenant kvcache budget temporarily on high-memory nodes, (3) add a metric for "seq_length_mismatch_rate" to surface this faster.
Priya: I'll add the metric and a dashboard tile. Mateo — can you draft a short postmortem note with timeline and the selector fix?
Mateo: Will do. Draft ready in 30m.
Alex: Thanks everyone. Leaving the thread open until postmortem + canary prove green. :thumbsup:
